questions.q: What does the global Search box at the top of the Fabric portal search by?
options: Item name, title, creator, tag, or workspace, across every workspace you have access to
Only item names within your currently open workspace
Only the names of Fabric administrators
Only items that have been Certified
questions.explain: Global search finds items by name, title, creator, tag, or workspace across the whole tenant, powered by Azure AI Search, and results are trimmed to what you're allowed to see.

questions.q: Why does discoverability matter as a governance control, not just a convenience?
options: It helps prevent duplicate 'shadow' data assets by letting people find existing items before rebuilding them
It automatically deletes items nobody has searched for in 90 days
It is required before any item can be assigned a sensitivity label
It replaces the need for row-level security
questions.explain: If people can't find what already exists, they rebuild it — producing untracked, unowned 'shadow' duplicates. Discoverability is the first defense against that sprawl.

questions.q: What is the OneLake catalog's Explore tab used for?
options: Browsing a filterable, tenant-wide list of every Fabric item you have access to, even when you don't know its exact name
Only viewing items you personally created
Editing tenant-wide security roles
Writing lineage documentation for a workspace
questions.explain: The Explore tab is the OneLake catalog's browse experience — a list of items across every workspace you can access, narrowed with selectors and filters like item type, tags, and workspace.

questions.q: Besides item type and workspace, which filter is specifically called out as the one that helps you avoid rebuilding something that already has an owner?
options: Owner
Sensitivity label
Refresh schedule
File size
questions.explain: Filtering by Owner tells you exactly who already owns an asset, so you can ask for access instead of quietly building a competing version.

questions.q: Which endorsement badge specifically means an organization-authorized reviewer verified the item meets the organization's quality standards?
options: Certified
Promoted
Favorited
Refreshed
questions.explain: Certified means an authorized reviewer verified the item against organizational standards. Promoted is just the creator's own opinion that it's ready for reuse; Lesson 18 covers both in depth.
